blocks.thai: พระเถระที่จะแสดงธรรมตั้งพัดให้อุโบสถศีล อุบาสกอุบาสิกาตั้งใจสมาทาน คือว่าตามพระโดยเคารพดังนี้
blocks.english: The elder who is to give the Dhamma talk sets up his fan to give the Uposatha precepts. The laymen and laywomen set their minds on undertaking them, repeating after the monk respectfully, as follows.

pages.note: The page opens with a prose instruction: the elder sets up his fan to give the precepts and the laypeople repeat after him. No heading above it.
The นะโม three times, then the refuge-going in three rounds. The book prints NO title over any of it. Footnote marker 1 on the last line.

blocks.thai: พระเถระว่า ติสะระณะคะมะนัง นิฏฐิตัง. อุบาสกอุบาสิการับพร้อมกันว่า อามะ ภันเต. พระเถระว่านำต่อไปดังนี้.
blocks.english: The elder says tisaraṇagamanaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ — 'the going to the three refuges is completed'. The laymen and laywomen answer together āma bhante — 'yes, venerable sir'. The elder then leads on as follows.

pages.note: Between the two chants: the elder declares the refuge-going completed, the assembly answers อามะ ภันเต, and the elder leads on.

blocks.note: A canonical citation, reproduced exactly as printed and NOT expanded. It is carried as a page footnote block rather than as source_printed on the chants, because ONE printed footnote serves TWO markers on this page and source_printed can only attach per chant — which would print the citation twice where the book prints it once.

pages.note: Heading อุโบสถศีล, the eight numbered precepts, then the unnumbered closing undertaking. Footnote marker 1 on precept 8. Below the rule at the foot, the page's only footnote: '1. ขุ.ขุ. 25/1-2'.

checks.issue: DECISION NEEDED. Verses 1-3 are the same นะโม line already in the app as 'pubbabhaga-namakara' on page 2. I have NOT treated this as a repeat, because the prompt's rule is that a printing which DIFFERS is not a repeat, and this one differs twice over: page 2 prints it with a closing full stop and page 12 does not, and here it runs straight on into the refuges as one act led by the elder rather than standing alone after its own invitation. A chant dict also carries only ONE page_start, so making it a repeat would leave page 12 in the app without the นะโม the book prints on it. Please confirm this is the right call — it will recur constantly across a book whose services overlap.
The book prints NO title for this passage. The id and the English title are mine; title_thai and title_pali are left empty rather than invented. Same treatment as 'pubbabhaga-namakara' on page 2.

Grouping the นะโม (verses 1-3) together with the refuge-going (verses 4-6) as ONE chant is my reading. The book separates them only by a line break, and closes the whole with ติสะระณะคะมะนัง นิฏฐิตัง, which names only the refuge-going. Splitting them into two chants is defensible and is your call.

FOOTNOTE, ONE SERVING TWO MARKERS. Page 12 prints a single footnote '1. ขุ.ขุ. 25/1-2' but TWO superscript 1 markers: one here on the last refuge line, one on precept 8 of อุโบสถศีล. The range fits both halves — Khuddakapāṭha 1 is the Saraṇattaya and 2 the Sikkhāpada. It is therefore carried as ONE page footnote block, not as source_printed on each chant, which would have printed the citation twice where the book prints it once. Neither chant carries source_printed as a result — say if you would rather the citation also hung off the chants for the study view.
ขุ.ขุ. abbreviates ขุททกนิกาย ขุททกปาฐะ — Khuddaka-nikāya, Khuddakapāṭha. Recorded here rather than in the field, because the reference is reproduced exactly as printed and never expanded.

Each refuge round is set as ONE printed line running Buddha, Dhamma, Saṅgha, so it is kept as one verse rather than split into three. Rounds 2 and 3 wrap onto a second line through justification only.

vocabulary.meaning: abstention — what the precept actually is: the refraining itself, undertaken, not a rule imposed from outside

vocabulary.pali: สิกขาปะทัง
vocabulary.meaning: a training rule; literally a 'step of training', one part of a path being learned

vocabulary.pali: สะมาทิยามิ
vocabulary.meaning: I undertake, I take upon myself — the first person of the act each precept consists of

vocabulary.pali: ปาณาติปาตา
vocabulary.meaning: from the destruction of breathing beings — the first precept, wider than 'killing people'

vocabulary.pali: อะทินนาทานา
vocabulary.meaning: from taking what is not given — the phrasing is broader than theft and covers anything not freely offered

vocabulary.pali: อะพ๎รัห๎มะจะริยา
vocabulary.meaning: from unchastity. On an Uposatha day the lay precept tightens from 'sexual misconduct' to full celibacy

vocabulary.pali: วิกาละโภชะนา
vocabulary.meaning: from eating at the wrong time — after midday until dawn, the monastic timing a layperson takes on for the day

vocabulary.pali: อุจจาสะยะนะมะหาสะยะนา
vocabulary.meaning: from high and large beds — luxurious sleeping places, the eighth factor

vocabulary.pali: พุทธะปัญญัตตัง
vocabulary.meaning: appointed by the Buddha — said of the Uposatha to mark it as laid down, not devised locally

vocabulary.pali: อัฏฐังคะสะมันนาคะตัง
vocabulary.meaning: endowed with eight factors — the Uposatha is complete only with all eight, not most of them
